role.altitude: The art therapist keeps photographing and choosing artwork, teaching, setting up showcases and planning trips around clients' needs; moving photos between devices, hunting for consent forms, typing labels and arranging bookings by phone shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the record's mobile app for photos and consent
role.ambitious_version: A therapist for whom every artwork is in the record with its consent status, and trips and showcases run from a checklist.

tasks.short: Photograph or videotape client artwork, add the photos to client records, check consent for promotional use, and prepare images for promotional purposes.

steps.what: Art therapist photographs or videotapes the client artwork
Art therapist transfers the photos to the computer and files them in client records
Art therapist checks the client's consent for promotional use
Art therapist selects and prepares images for promotional purposes: crops and removes names

tasks.design: The therapist photographs artwork with the client record's mobile app, which stores each photo in the right client record with date and session, instead of moving files from a camera to a computer and naming them. Consent for promotional use is recorded once in the record and shown next to each photo, instead of looking up paper forms. Photographing and choosing images for promotion stay with the therapist. Photos stay on the record, not on the device.
tasks.previous_blocker: Photos moved by memory card and consent sat on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile apps of client records that capture photos into the record.
tasks.still_hard: Large or three-dimensional work that needs several angles or video.
tasks.human_edge: Photographing the work so it shows what the client meant.

reach.learn: Whether artwork photos are in the record the same day.

evidence.claim: Mobile apps of client records capture photos straight into the record.
Therapy artwork in a client record is health data; promotional use needs explicit consent.

assumptions: Boundary: photographing and filing artwork; documenting sessions (task 19151) and showcases (task 19156) are sibling tasks.
Photographing and preparing promotional images keep most of their time.
unknowns: Whether the record has a mobile app.
research_questions: Are photos missing from records less often?

incremental.description: Art therapist records consent status in the record once per client.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: video and many angles; high: flat work photographed in the app.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare workshop material, teach and demonstrate art therapy techniques or processes to artists, interns, volunteers or others, and give feedback on their practice.

steps.what: Art therapist prepares workshop material and exercises
Art therapist teaches and demonstrates art therapy techniques or processes
Art therapist gives feedback on participants' practice

tasks.design: Workshop material and exercises are kept in a shared library by technique and audience, so the therapist adapts earlier material instead of starting each workshop from scratch. Teaching and feedback stay fully personal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material was made again for each workshop.
tasks.human_edge: Showing how a technique feels from the client's side.

evidence.claim: Shared material libraries cut repeat preparation.

assumptions: Boundary: teaching art therapy techniques; in-service workshops for other professionals (task 19155) and supervising interns (task 19162) are sibling tasks.
Teaching and feedback keep their full time.

incremental.description: Art therapist files new material in the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new topics each time; high: repeat workshops.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select artwork with clients and get consent, book the venue, make labels, write, check and send invitations, and set up art showcases to display artwork produced by clients.

steps.what: Art therapist selects artwork with clients and gets their consent to display it
Art therapist books the venue and plans the date
Art therapist makes labels and the list of works
Art therapist writes the invitation
Art therapist checks the final invitation and guest list
Art therapist sends the invitation to the guest list
Art therapist sets up the art showcase and displays the artwork

tasks.design: Selecting work and getting consent stay with the therapist and the client. A showcase checklist with earlier venues and contacts shortens booking. Labels and the list of works are printed from one list in a template, showing only the name form each client agreed to. The invitation starts from the last one, and the therapist checks text and guest list and sends that version by mail merge instead of one by one. Setting up stays hands-on.
tasks.previous_blocker: Labels and invitations were typed one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates filled from a list and mail merge.
tasks.still_hard: Clients who change their mind about showing work.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a client feel proud rather than exposed.
tasks.altitude: Less typing; selecting and setting up stay.

evidence.claim: Templates filled from a list produce labels and mail-merged invitations.

assumptions: Boundary: coordinating showcases; photographing artwork (task 19152) is a sibling task.
Selecting, consent, checking and setting up keep their full time.
research_questions: Is preparation time per showcase lower?

incremental.description: Art therapist keeps the showcase checklist and guest list current.

approvals.approved_version: The invitation text and guest list as checked by the therapist in s5; any edit needs a new check before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small showcase; high: a yearly showcase with many works and guests.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose the museum and plan around the group's needs, book tickets and accessible transport, collect consent and accessibility details, write, check and send trip information to coordinate field trips for client groups.

steps.what: Art therapist chooses the museum or display and plans the trip around the group's needs
Art therapist books museum tickets and accessible transport
Art therapist collects client consent and accessibility and medical details
Art therapist writes the trip information for clients, carers and staff
Art therapist checks the final trip information and the recipient list
Art therapist sends the trip information to clients, carers and staff

approvals.approved_version: The trip information text and the recipient list as checked by the therapist in s5; any edit needs a new check before sending.

tasks.design: Choosing the museum and planning around the group stay with the therapist. Group tickets are booked online where the museum offers it, and accessible transport through the regular provider's booking form, instead of by phone. Consent and accessibility details are recorded on a trip form in the client record; medical details are visible only to the staff on the trip. Trip information starts from a template, and the therapist checks text and recipients and sends that version to clients, carers and staff in one go.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bookings were made by phone and forms collected on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Online group booking, trip forms in the record and message templates.
tasks.still_hard: Museums without step-free access or group booking.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which client will be overwhelmed in a busy hall.

evidence.claim: Museums offer online group booking and record forms capture consent and access needs.
Medical and accessibility details are health data and are shown only to staff who need them.

assumptions: Boundary: coordinating trips; showcases (task 19156) are a sibling task.
Input contract for s2: about 60% of museums visited offer online group booking; s2 is priced at that share.
Planning and checking keep their full time.
research_questions: Do trips run with complete consent more often?

incremental.description: Art therapist keeps the trip template and transport contacts current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: museums without online booking; high: regular venues with online group booking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
